newsitem.title: UK: UK/BENELUX PETROL PRICES RAISED ON MOGAS GAINS.
newsitem.headline: UK/BENELUX PETROL PRICES RAISED ON MOGAS GAINS.

text.p: Oil companies raised petrol prices in the U.K. and all the Benelux countries on Wednesday amidst continent-wide efforts to recoup rapidly rising gasoline prices.

British Petroleum Co. plc said it had raised its U.K. pump prices by 2 pence a litter effective Wednesday as Shell said it had raised its wholesale prices by 2 pence and Esso said it would seek to raise its prices in line with hikes by other suppliers.
Supermarket chain and petrol retailer, Asda Plc, said it would maintain its policy of keeping its petrol prices 4 percent below the national average.

Belgian petrol prices were meanwhile raised Wednesday by BEF1.10 a litre, a move described by Peter Regnier of Oil Price Assessments Ltd (OPAL) as the biggest non-tax related pump price hike in Belgium for 25 years.

The Belgian increase took the level for premium unleaded 95 Ron gasoline at the pump to BEF38.50 as the Netherlands saw a 2 cents gain to NLG2.24 and Luxembourg also registered an LUF1.10 rise, Regnier said.

An Esso Hamburg spokesman said German pump prices had been raised as many as 20 times so far this year, although fierce competition among suppliers had led to most if not all of those gains being wiped out.
Regnier said German and Dutch pump prices had been raised six times in the past two months, adding that a further Dutch increase was expected by this weekend.
Italian oil firms earlier Wednesday bowed to government pressure by saying they would freeze pump prices for at least eight days, having Tuesday announced hikes of ITL5.0 a litre.
BP, Shell and Esso all said the U.K. increases were a response to recent strong gains in the international gasoline market as one U.K. oil company source indicated further hikes could be forthcoming.
"Two pence is probably not enough; more increased are needed to make up for a $25 a tonne rise in gasoline prices during July alone, so more increases could be in the pipeline," the source said.

The scale of recent physical gasoline price gains were underlined earlier Wednesday by a $240.25 FOB AR deal for prompt premium unleaded gasoline, the highest recorded level since the 1990/91 Gulf War.

While U.K. oil majors and petrol retailers also point to wafer thin margins since Esso introduced its Pricewatch scheme in January 1996, continental suppliers have more recently seen their margins squeezed by a combination of rising dollar prices and rapid gains in the dollar's value against their currencies.
